title: Perissodactyls are more closely related to hares and rabbits than to other ungulates

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Perissodactyls are more closely related to hares and rabbits than to other ungulates

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Since the rabbit's skull is derived from that of a primitive rhinoceros by a simple uniform downward flexure, the Perissodactyla are more closely related to the Leporidae than to other ungulates, and the Leporidae more closely to Perissodactyla than to other rodents.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVII: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For my part, I would go further; for I think there is strong reason to believe that the Perissodactyles are more closely related to the Leporidae than the former are to the other Ungulates, or than the Leporidae are to the rest of the Rodentia.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVII, “On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms”; topic “Perissodactyl and rabbit skulls”. Scope: phylogenetic relationships of Perissodactyla, Leporidae, other ungulates and rodents

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch17-13: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.98

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The relationship is an explicit topology and abundant public molecular data directly discriminate it from alternatives. Standard phylogenomic analyses can resolve the claim across the full named groups now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the placement of Leporidae and Perissodactyla in large independent molecular and genomic phylogenies. A topology nesting each with its accepted close relatives rather than with one another refutes the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Deep-time topology can vary by locus, though not enough to make this proposed relationship competitive.

fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.95

data existence: 1.0
discriminating power: 0.98

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a phylogenetic hypothesis about named living clades, and those clades are densely sampled in public trees built from molecular data independent of the skull transformation. A small team can read the relationship off existing syntheses in days. That is a direct confirm-or-refute test of the relatedness statement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Place Perissodactyla, other ungulates, Leporidae and other rodents on genome-based trees and test the two sister-group claims: perissodactyls closer to rabbits than to other ungulates, and rabbits closer to perissodactyls than to other rodents. Either grouping is refuted if the credible trees put perissodactyls with other laurasiatheres and rabbits with rodents.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The skull-flexure argument that motivated the claim is a separate morphological question and is not settled by the tree alone.

Deep mammal nodes still differ in a few published studies, though the Glires versus Laurasiatheria split is repeatedly recovered.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: If the claim holds, Perissodactyla and Leporidae form a clade in the current synthetic mammal phylogeny that excludes the other ungulates (Artiodactyla; also Proboscidea and Hyracoidea in the 1917 sense of Ungulata) and excludes the rodents.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: Resolved the 20 pre-registered species to OTT ids with the Open Tree TNRS, requested the induced subtree of the current synthetic tree (synth opentree16.1), parsed the Newick, and found the smallest clade containing all three perissodactyl and all three leporid tips. Sub-claim 1 was scored by whether that clade contains artiodactyl tips, sub-claim 2 by whether it contains rodent tips; the smallest clades for perissodactyls+artiodactyls and leporids+rodents were also extracted. NCBI Taxonomy lineages were fetched by E-utilities and intersected to find named clades shared by Perissodactyla and Leporidae but not by Artiodactyla or Rodentia.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Take the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree (induced_subtree API, current synth version) over these tips: Perissodactyla = Equus caballus, Ceratotherium simum, Tapirus terrestris; other ungulates = Bos taurus, Sus scrofa, Camelus dromedarius (Artiodactyla), Loxodonta africana (Proboscidea), Procavia capensis (Hyracoidea); Leporidae = Oryctolagus cuniculus, Lepus europaeus, Sylvilagus floridanus; other lagomorph = Ochotona princeps; Rodentia = Mus musculus, Rattus norvegicus, Sciurus carolinensis, Cavia porcellus, Castor canadensis; outgroups = Canis lupus, Homo sapiens, Monodelphis domestica. Let C be the smallest clade containing all perissodactyl and all leporid tips. Sub-claim 1 (perissodactyls closer to leporids than to other ungulates) holds iff C contains no artiodactyl tip; sub-claim 2 (leporids closer to perissodactyls than to other rodents) holds iff C contains no rodent tip. Supports if both hold. Independent check: NCBI Taxonomy lineages (efetch) must place Perissodactyla and Leporidae in a shared named clade below Boreoeutheria that excludes Artiodactyla and Rodentia.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Refutes if C contains both artiodactyl and rodent tips, i.e. perissodactyls nest with other ungulates and leporids nest with rodents rather than with each other (and NCBI Taxonomy places Perissodactyla in Laurasiatheria with Artiodactyla and Leporidae in Glires with Rodentia). Mixed if exactly one sub-claim holds.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: tips (of 20) in the smallest Open Tree clade containing all perissodactyl and leporid tips; it is Boreoeutheria and includes all artiodactyl, rodent, carnivore and primate tips

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: topology from a synthesis of published phylogenies; no branch support values in the synthetic tree

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson's 'more closely related' is read as phylogenetic proximity (more recent common ancestry), the standard modern meaning and the one his transformation argument invokes. 'Other ungulates' is taken in the 1917 sense (Artiodactyla, with Proboscidea and Hyracoidea also included and reported separately); 'other rodents' means Rodentia, since lagomorphs were then classed as rodents (Duplicidentata). The Open Tree synthesis integrates published molecular phylogenies independent of the skull-shape argument; NCBI Taxonomy is a curated classification, not an independent inference, and is used only as a consistency check.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
Open Tree of Life synthetic tree, induced subtree over 20 mammal tips (API v3)

NCBI Taxonomy lineages for Perissodactyla, Leporidae, Artiodactyla, Rodentia, Lagomorpha (E-utilities)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The Open Tree synthetic tree carries no support values; however the groupings that refute the claim (Perissodactyla with Artiodactyla and Carnivora in Laurasiatheria; Leporidae with Ochotonidae and Rodentia in Glires) are recovered by every large molecular phylogenomic study of placental mammals and are encoded in NCBI Taxonomy, which is a curated classification rather than an independent analysis.

Thompson's claim was framed as an inference from a Cartesian transformation of skull outlines; the test addresses only its phylogenetic conclusion, not whether the skull transformation itself is geometrically simple.

Proboscidea and Hyracoidea (ungulates in the 1917 sense) fall in Afrotheria, outside the clade shared by perissodactyls and leporids, so for those 'other ungulates' sub-claim 1 would hold trivially; the sub-claim fails for the Artiodactyla, the ungulates Thompson's comparison (horses, rhinoceroses vs other hoofed mammals) most directly concerns.

The induced-subtree Newick is saved under data/ and its SHA-256 recorded; re-running against a later synth version may change the version string but not the result unless mammalian phylogeny is overturned.
